content:
## _Nishas VN, a senior game character artist with over 7 years in the industry and 2 years in graphic design, highlights her expertise in her latest project, Odin Alfiifir._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/2c97a676ece343eab833be53c87d087b79809f6c388744499fea437788232916.jpeg)

# **Interview with NISHAS VN | Odin | Character Artist**

# **Artist introduction**

My name is Nishas VN. I'm a senior game character artist with more than 7 years of experience in the Game industry and 2 years experience in graphic design . I've worked on quite a lot of games during the years with the last one being Alan Wake 2.

# **When did you start using Marvelous Designer and how did that affect your workflow process?**

Seven years ago, I ventured into the world of Marvelous Designer. My journey began by immersing myself in online tutorials on YouTube, gradually uncovering its immense potential. This software has revolutionized the fashion and 3D design industries by enabling the creation of lifelike 3D clothing and fabric simulations. Not only confined to fashion, but Marvelous Designer has also started making waves in the realm of gaming. Its integration into games, like the renowned Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain by Konami and Kojima Productions, showcased the software's versatility and impact beyond traditional design spheres. Witnessing its application in such high-profile projects piqued my interest and solidified my belief in its far-reaching influence.

Marvelous Designer has remarkably streamlined my workflow, replacing time-consuming traditional cloth sculpting with hyper-realistic garments in mere minutes. Its extensive library of fabrics allows for the authentic capture of cloth materials, elevating the realism of designs. Moreover, Marvelous Designer not only enhances cloth creation but also significantly expedites other processes, such as high-poly and low-poly UV mapping, ultimately saving valuable time across multiple facets of the design pipeline.

# **As a student, how much time did you find sufficient to gain confidence in using Marvelous Designer?**

I was pleasantly surprised by how easy it was to start using Marvelous Designer, and within a month, I was able to achieve some results. However, to produce high-quality work, you must invest more time in learning shortcuts, selecting the appropriate tool for each situation, and researching information for the tools you are unfamiliar with. If you take a break from using Marvelous Designer for some time, it can feel like starting from scratch again.

# **Explain the project's creation aspects, including intentions, goals, cloth design approach, and references.**

Let me delve into my recent project featuring Odin Alfiifir. This endeavor posed unique challenges, particularly in clothing design, prompting me to explore Marvelous Designer's capabilities beyond traditional garment creation. I aimed to showcase a versatility for readers' benefit In this venture, Marvelous Designer played a pivotal role, not only in crafting the clothing but also in designing elements like the bag, cape, and boots. Often overlooked, Marvelous Designer's prowess extends beyond typical clothing design; it aided me in achieving remarkable results, notably in crafting authentic leather boots. Many tend to underestimate its ability to create such intricate details, opting for sculpting methods that often result in unnatural folds. Marvelous Designer, however, provides a more intuitive and realistic approach to crafting these elements.

Prior to diving into the creative process, gathering references is a crucial step. For my personal projects, I typically blend design freedom with inspiration rather than strictly adhering to a specific concept or reference. For this particular endeavor, I drew from a Norse Viking dress as a foundation, embellishing it with numerous additional elements to seamlessly integrate it into a fantastical setting. This approach allowed me to infuse elements of my imagination while retaining the essence of the original Norse design.

In my PureRef canvas, I curated a diverse array of costume concept and prop inspirations. This compilation served as a rich tapestry of ideas, guiding me to craft a design that strikes a balance between cohesion and distinctiveness. The goal was to create a unified yet uniquely individualized piece, drawing from various sources to inspire a cohesive and original design.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/c00c834a91a8460f8a65cc66d31e47ad7a7a414fea374a61b7d3c740ea07bd52.jpeg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/f5c7ac5928484c559aa9e4541d0357c9Odin_2-1.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/651f26ee639a426d9ca9dc2d6dece379Odin_2-4.webp)

Once I've determined the direction for my creation, it's time to import the base mesh or avatar. While many opt for default avatars in Marvelous Designer, I prefer a more controlled approach. It's crucial to have greater influence and control, as clothing inherently influences the form of the underlying flesh. This detail often gets overlooked. Therefore, sculpting any potential influence is essential to ensure a seamless integration between the clothing and the body underneath.

From my experience, I've learned that achieving realistic clothing hinges greatly on the initial fitting of the garments. It's crucial to focus on clean patterns and precise fitting as natural stitching and realistic folds tend to emerge more natural during simulation. I advise limiting the use of pins to necessities, as excessive pinning and forced folds can contribute to an unrealistic feel in the clothing. To maintain authenticity steer clear of excessive pinching or symmetrical folds, aiming instead for balanced and natural drapery. Additionally, when dealing with layered clothing, it's advisable to avoid utilizing the fast (GPU) simulation, Due to complications with layered garments, it's best to avoid utilizing the (GPU) simulation, as it may not effectively handle the complexities inherent in layered clothing.

Many decorative elements such as ornaments and weapons were deliberately excluded from Marvelous Designer, as their impact on the clothing simulation was minimal. Hence, I chose not to import these details into Marvelous Designer, opting to address them separately outside the software.

# **Share your approach to working with Marvelous Designer. What tricks have you discovered to boost efficiency, and what advice would you offer to new users?**

Prior to diving into the task at hand, I make it a point to set up the lighting meticulously. Getting the lighting just right is crucial as it significantly amplifies the overall appearance and visibility of folds and wrinkles in the design.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/8368958edd934304a4ea5589d415045dScreenshot_01.png)

**Constructing the boot**

I adopt a different approach in crafting boots by initially sculpting a base model in ZBrush, which I later import into Marvelous Designer. Using this base mesh as a guide, I employ the Line tool to delineate the boot's outline, refining it further with the Flatten tool to generate a visible pattern, reflecting in the 2D pattern window. Once the entire boot design is established, I simulate its appearance, utilizing the ZBrush base mesh as the avatar mesh within Marvelous Designer. This methodology allows for precise control over achieving the desired fold Mixture in the design.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/165611acb0f64fd0989ffdb63b952fc0Screenshot_02.png)

My workflow within Marvelous Designer follows a clear path. Initially, I focused on constructing a clean pattern and stitching to generate a blockout file with high particle distance. This blockout serves as the foundation, aimed at refining the fitting precisely without relying on excessive pinching or excess fabric. Once the primary fit is perfected, I progress to the secondary detail stage, decreasing the particle distance to introduce moderate folds and simulate additional intricacies. Finally, in the temporary detail phase, I set a low particle distance to add the final touches and meticulously finalize the file.

# **Explain your process of moving between Marvelous Designer and other software. How do you prepare your project for a smooth transition?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/498f532ec867455ea2e12420607be5c0Screenshot_03.png)

To convert the Marvelous Designer file into a clean topology, I utilize Maya's Transfer Attributes tool. After exporting, I save two sets of files named boot3D and boot2D. The boot3D file is the direct export from Marvelous Designer, while the boot2D represents the 2D pattern version obtained by right-clicking and selecting "Reset 2D Arrangement." Next, I import the boot2D file into Maya and proceed to create a clean topology using either the Quadraw tool or by employing ZRemesher in ZBrush. Once the retopology process is complete, I save the file as bootretopo. To finalize the transformation, I configure the Transfer AMibutes settings accordingly through the tool's options.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/c931aadfc1e94a71833ea073a7b63a98Screenshot_04.png)

Following the retopology process, select the boot2D file first, then the boot retopology file in Maya. Utilize the Transfer Attributes tool and click "Apply" to transfer the UVs from boot2D to boot retopology. Once the transfer is complete, adjust the Transfer Attributes settings as needed to ensure the seamless transfer of UVs between the files.

Afterward, right-click and choose "Smooth" to increase the subdivision of the boot reæpo in Maya. Following this, select the boot 3D file first, then the boot reæpo file, and click "Apply" in the Transfer Attributes tool. This action directly transfers the boot retopo attributes to the boot3D file. Next, clear any history by selecting "Edit" and then "Delete by Type > History." You can proceed to remove both the boot3D and boot2D meshes. Export and save the boot retopo mesh. Subsequently, import it into ZBrush and access the Geometry tab, selecting Edge Loop > Panel Loops. Employing this function provides thickness to the boot. Apply "Reconstruit" to revert to lower subdivisions, resulting in a refined and clean high-poly boot mesh.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/a89db3439fff40b09687b1ac1f72c0e7/images/f55df1ed216649838dce7bc36508779bScreenshot_05.png)

# **_by Nishas VN_**  
[** _ArtStation_**](https://www.artstation.com/nishas)
content_description: Showcasing senior game character artist Nishas VN’s expert workflow and creative process using Marvelous Designer to craft realistic, high-quality 3D clothing and accessories for the Odin Alfiifir project.

title: Pioneer of Marvelous Designer for Digital Sculpting
content:
## _Masato Ohata, active since 2013, discusses digital sculpting, his creative process, and insights from his new book STRING, blending art and entertainment._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/0a1bc98b210744cf803dc1b0ad38787c002.jpg)

# **Interview with Masato Ohata | Pioneer of Marvelous Designer for Digital Sculpting | Figure Sculptor**

Masato Ohata has been active as a sculptor since 2013, engaging in various forms of entertainment production, including commercial prototypes and original figure production, as well as character design both domestically and internationally in Japan. In this interview, we delve into his insights on digital sculpting and explore the behind-the-scenes stories of his works featured in his newly released book, "STRING".

# **Could you please briefly introduce yourself?**

I am a figure sculptor, Masato Ohata. I started producing original figures three years after becoming a prototype sculptor, and since then, I have been active in both commercial prototypes and original works. I've also had the opportunity to do character design work, and recently, I was in charge of character design for the puppet show "Fantarne!" broadcasted on NHK.

# 

# **Please tell us about your recently released book, "STRING Masato Ohata Artworks & Sculpting Techniques".**

It is my second art book. It features original sculptural works I have produced over the past six years since the release of my first art book. I also created a new piece titled "BREAKING FREE" for the cover of the book.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/b765a58547e34028a3580f25ccd17f23001.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/d99f7b6d352b42eeb321e865363bb582002.jpg)

# **How did you use Marvelous Designer in your sculpting process?**

Since I started producing original sculptures, I have been using Marvelous Designer mainly for simulating clothing and fabric for figures. It allows me to express wrinkles, textures, and thicknesses of clothing that match the poses of the figures. Specifically, I create the figure's body first, then design the clothing, and use Marvelous Designer's basic avatar to drape the clothing. After that, I adjust the clothing data in ZBrush by exporting it as an OBJ file.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/0933f7b1e7d34c1390dcdbf7c87402ab003.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/2249aa8de7e144d0a10c81269b2dafe7004.jpg)

# **Do you have any tips or precautions for digital sculpting with the intention of 3D printing?**

One of the most important considerations for 3D printing is managing the thickness of the model. I use the thickness option in ZBrush's dynamic sub-division, but before that, I need to convert the clothing objects created in Marvelous Designer into quadrilateral polygons. I used a plugin to convert triangular polygons to quadrilateral polygons in ZBrush, which I purchased from ArtStation. However, I heard that the latest version of Marvelous Designer allows for topology editing, which is very convenient.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/eee48c2deb9c4d60884103b8185d79ea005.jpg)

# **If there is a favorite moment during your digital sculpting process, please share.**

The moment when the envisioned image is materialized into a sculpture is the most enjoyable for me. By using tools such as 3D scanning, Marvelous Designer, and various simulation software, I can create sculptures that exceed my abilities and imagination. However, the most important thing is not "what tools to use" but "how to express." I aim to experience and refine my sculpting skills by trying out various tools and software and opening up new horizons as an artist. The most enjoyable moment is when I feel that I have achieved that goal, even if only slightly.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/fa15a7e9fca64e16b161db4d733df532006.jpg)

# **If there is a favorite moment during your digital sculpting process, please share.**

The moment when the envisioned image is materialized into a sculpture is the most enjoyable for me. By using tools such as 3D scanning, Marvelous Designer, and various simulation software, I can create sculptures that exceed my abilities and imagination. However, the most important thing is not "what tools to use" but "how to express." I aim to experience and refine my sculpting skills by trying out various tools and software and opening up new horizons as an artist. The most enjoyable moment is when I feel that I have achieved that goal, even if only slightly.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/fa15a7e9fca64e16b161db4d733df532006.jpg)

# **If there is a memorable piece or expression that you created using Marvelous Designer, please introduce it.**

The cover artwork "GAME" from my art book released six years ago was a memorable piece for me because it introduced Marvelous Designer's clothing-making technique to many people in the sculpting field at a time when it was not widely known among figure sculptors. Also, the sculpting of the veil in my recent work "言霊" would not have been possible without Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/81aa342d35fe4652b456c4802e5e37bb007.jpg)

# **Are there any new features you would like to see implemented in Marvelous Designer?**

Since I have been using the perpetual version of Marvelous Designer for several years, I am constantly amazed by the features of the latest version. One feature I think would be great is the ability to import models created in external DCC tools and convert them into Marvelous Designer avatars (including automatic rigging). This would be very useful for figure production. Although there are some limitations in the simulation, such as wrinkles generated due to particle spacing, I think it would be interesting to have variation presets for directions in which wrinkles are more likely to occur. Since I am not yet proficient in utilizing all the features of the latest version of Marvelous Designer, I plan to study and enjoy exploring the various functions!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e465e14215594dd188fe10f7d6b29529/images/b9248a20d35c41da858dd5b44a48f6ac6a7ad82c55e14bd18eaa3a0364f56dbb.jpg)
content_description: Explore Masato Ohata’s innovative digital sculpting techniques, creative insights, and the artistic journey behind his new book *STRING*, showcasing the fusion of Marvelous Designer and 3D figure artistry.

GDC 2024 has just wrapped up and we thoroughly enjoyed our time there, meeting game developers, artists, students, and our partners! Before the memories fade, here's a brief recap of our experience in San Francisco.

# **Unreal Engine x Marvelous Designer: Announcements (March 20th)**

![3301111669c243fba10077f8e512b155](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202510/86e67c2c973e47538d800b5e7913fafa/images/3301111669c243fba10077f8e512b155GDC2024.jpg)

We made a major announcement at Epic Games's State of Unreal 2024 address: following a year-long partnership, we're excited to announce the Marvelous Designer Integration in UE 5.4: a new USD workflow for Marvelous Designer and UE/UEFN. 

As part of the announcement our very own Bryan Kim, Software Product Manager for Marvelous Designer, took the stage, speaking to our continued collaboration with Epic Games and the development of their latest Talisman demo on UE 5.4. 

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zcn02-buMsQ?start=13286

 _Say goodbye to limited clothing options with MetaHuman. It's time to elevate your MetaHuman to a new level of realism and accuracy with Marvelous Designer._

Thanks to our joint efforts, starting from UE 5.4, creators can now apply more dynamic clothing to your MetaHumans in UEFN through the updated USD export for garments, including geometry, materials, and the necessary data for simulation setup. Customize the appearance of your MetaHuman more easily than ever with Marvelous Designer! 

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HBnsp_IuZ_c?start=0

Within the Talisman demo, we observe the MetaHuman dressed in specialized dynamic clothing created with Marvelous Designer, underscoring the pivotal role of custom attire in shaping the narrative of your game. This personalized ensemble significantly contributes to the convincing narrative of your game. 

In UE 5.4, cloth physics isn't limited to clothing alone; it also allows for the customization of environmental assets using Marvelous Designer, which can then be imported into UEFN.

*As a UEFN creator, you will be eligible for a free one-year license of Marvelous Designer to create dynamic clothing using the new UE5.4 workflow, which can then be imported into UEFN projects. Further updates will be provided through @FNCreate, commencing in late April. Licenses can be obtained within a two-month window after sign-up registration opens.

title: Chladni
content:
## _In Chladni, sound shapes a unique world. Timothy Motion utilized Marvelous Designer’s fast fabric simulations and creative tools to bring this vision to life._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1979a148430b44829bcaad763f0bef7c/images/b5939749eba5468aa1d38ed5e827acf676d02207a06d4a45aed72d77f08081a3.png)

# **Interview with Timothy Motion | Chladni﻿ | Art Director**

# **We'd like to get to know you better, can you tell us a little about yourself?**

Timothy:

the head of Timothy Motion and producer of CHLADNI, established the Timothy Motion in Taipei in 2013. Comprised of a passionate group of young individuals, Timothy Motion is a creative team known for its diverse and magnificent style of work. Each creation delivers an astonishing visual feast, garnering numerous awards both domestically and internationally. Have spearheaded several major projects in Taiwan, including multiple Golden Bell Awards, the World University Games, League of Legends (LOL), and ASUS events. Timothy Motion is recognized as a comprehensive visual production company.

Xite: Concept Designer / Art Director。

Specialized in 3D visual arts, abstract concept visualization, character design, and creating atmospheres for scenes and world-building. Often interprets religious art through digital art. Has been involved in various music video productions and executed visual projects for renowned brands. Notable visual projects include contributions to the Golden Melody Awards, Golden Bell Awards ceremony animations, participation in MV productions for various Korean artists and Kpop groups, promotional videos for SM Entertainment in Korea, OZI album production, MVs for Sunset Rollercoaster and Bisiugroup, and animation design for the League of Legends Spirit Blossom Festival. In addition to commercial projects, has engaged in conceptual art creation, with personal works earning nominations in multiple international film festivals and winning the 2018 Red Dot Design Award.

# **Tell us about the project - Chladni**

In a world called Chladni, everything is governed by sound frequencies. All things are influenced by the patterns of audio vibrations, developing diverse ecosystems, cultures, and religions. Chladni functions like a living organism, with the pulsating rhythms of audio impacting the flow of energy in this world, creating a unique ecological system. The atmosphere, bodies of water, and mountains are all influenced and incorporate the behavior of audio waves.

Deceased life forms sprout lichen flowers (fungi) with audio wave patterns, decomposing and returning to nature, as no life can resist the influence. Most animals develop organs with audio wave patterns, and the Chladni people are naturally attuned to the flow of audio. This innate quality led the Chladni to invent devices that can concrete audio for communication after significant technological advancements. This allowed the naturally audio-sensitive population to communicate more efficiently and master technology derived from audio.

Communication using audio masks requires special locks to seal off the five Senses besides hearing, enabling users to concentrate on perceiving audio. This method is highly efficient, and conveyed information becomes more data-driven. Over several generations, the ability to express emotions by using facial features disappeared, leading to increased alienation among individuals. Those in distress cannot cry, and all emotions cannot be expressed directly, making mutual understanding more challenging. Conflict persists among individuals unable to express emotions, and the community gradually descends into fragmentation.

With the emotions lacking, people can not build strong relationships, neither or true love, and gradually, even marriage ceremonies are canceled.

somewhere in Chladni, there is a tribe of sound waves. Zaid and Cali are rare true loves in the tribe, but Cali's unexpected death prevents the two from being united. So Zaid requests the elders to grant him a wedding ring and not stop him from entering the fire purification at the funeral ceremony. He hopes to fulfill the commitment to marry Cali under the witness of the gods, even though this ceremony has been forgotten.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1979a148430b44829bcaad763f0bef7c/images/4dbe9ee187294e55b8746f3f54ca317328bc83cb32544206b24b8e8260cd69c9.png)

Zaid becomes the executor of this funeral ceremony, bringing Cali through the river full of corpses to the city of furnaces where bodies can be purified. Looking at the ring box in his hand, Zaid is determined to pass through the flames to reach the temple of Cladni. In the end, under the witness of the gods, Zaid uses the special ring to complete the wedding ceremony. Whether it is his persistence in love that touches the gods or his strong longing, the genetic lock binding the Chladni people is opened. He successfully opens his eyes and regains the ability to express emotions.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

Marvelous Designer allows for quick simulation of various fabric effects without retopology model, compensating for the manpower shortage issue of the rigging. Additionally, it enables rapid modification of clothing patterns in coordination with concept artists, saving a significant amount of time and cost.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1979a148430b44829bcaad763f0bef7c/images/4b6887af527b4866971f855619eee220a1d6faf9f4d24bd8846084578738b6f0.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/1979a148430b44829bcaad763f0bef7c/images/ae214cafabf34826a0cdc298a8c9807b16ddf8e3de0b4ec192b1d20174014f35.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

We also use Marmoset Toolbag4/Maya/SubstancePainter/Photoshop in clothing production.

Special thanks to the UV feature built into Marvelous Designer, which helps with subsequent texture painting in Substance Painter.

When exporting models with animations from other 3D software, remember not to have keyframes on joints regarding position information.

content:
## _Discover Bien Cordialement, a captivating clip by Alex, a French motion designer and 3D artist, blending diverse techniques with a unified artistic vision._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/21ab76b17bdb4c8abb28d96b7a4e52e5/images/8d1ff201edc64f9295175cf366ae3f6093371609cb394ae5be2f449f3ea9754f.png)

# **We'd like to learn more about you. Can you introduce yourself?**

Hello, my name is Alexandre. I'm a french motion designer and 3D artist, I'm currently working at ac3studio and I live in Paris. I graduated with a master's in art direction and motion design in 2020.

# **Your project, Bien Cordialement, is quite captivating and enjoyable. Could you elaborate more on the details of your project?**

I'm very pleased that you liked the "Bien cordialement" clip, which is a special project for me. When I did this project, it was to have not only a showreel, but also a project showing a wide range of skills and a coherent artistic direction throughout.

The lyrics are a satire of a cover letter.

I told myself that once the project was finished I'd start looking for a new job, so that's what I did, and it worked.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How has it contributed to your art direction?**

When I started this project, I quickly realized that I'd like to add some characters. Since I work mainly with Houdini, I tend to want to give everything an organic feel. That's why I told myself I wanted clothes with simulations. So I learned Marvelous Designer to make this project.

When I designed my characters I was inspired by cartoon characters, for example, the shapes of my characters' heads say a lot about their personalities.

So when I added clothes to my characters, I was able to sublimate them and really bring them to life. Clothes bring a unique look and personality to each of my characters.

# **Have you encountered any challenges in creating clothing and animation for stylized avatars?**

Yes, I did encounter some difficulties, because during this project I was learning marvelous at the same time, and I had to find the right workflow to go from Houdini to marvelous.

It's very easy to make a simple t-shirt on Marvelous Designer on standard humanoid characters (daz etc).

However, on my characters that aren't physically correct (if you give one of my characters a pentalon, the pentalon can't physically fit on him). On top of that, there are rig problems during their animations. This complicates the task, but Marvelous offers solutions for non-standard characters, and I hope they'll continue to develop their software in this direction.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/21ab76b17bdb4c8abb28d96b7a4e52e5/images/ed3aa25f25044c44a03911a1ace66ca362f8e68f6e3e492db7420af21a4949c4.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/21ab76b17bdb4c8abb28d96b7a4e52e5/images/ad6d50262d69471094ab135339ecd68214336564cc984596b1b2b8c037f08cf2.jpg)

The workflow began with semi-procedural character modeling on Houdini. Then add a rig and animation on Mixamo. Then I imported the character in A-pose on marvelous. So I could create and adjust his avatar and clothes.

Once I was satisfied with the clothes and the Mixamo animation reworked in Houdini. All I had to do was find a way to import the animation into Marvelous Designer.

To do this, I always added a blend of the A pose to the animation.

So the character with the animation starting in A pose on marvelous already has all his clothes perfectly fitted, as if he'd just stepped out of the tailor's!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/21ab76b17bdb4c8abb28d96b7a4e52e5/images/baf95f41fea8407dbc4404ff207fd889e24fa8d34b68461bb9c32bec641df649.jpg)

Then all I had to do was simulate the clothes on Marvelous Designer.

It's a very practical workflow because as long as you import the character in A pose in frame 1, the clothes will always be adjusted.

# **Lastly, what tips do you have for animators using Marvelous Designer?**

My tips for beginners: start simply with the classic t-shirt and pantaloon, and once you're satisfied, add more details.

If you're using a custom avatar, try to get as close as possible to the standard size.

Also creating the Bounding Volume and Arrangement Point on your own avatar in the Avatar Editor will be very helpful for arrangement.

For animations, play with the quality of the simulation, it's not because you make the simulation with high parameters that you'll get the result you want.

Last but not least, marvelous is simple and efficient for beginners. Once you've understood the workflow, have fun!

title: My Grandma
content:
## _Geumbi, a Korean character modeler, honored her grandmother through the heartfelt project My Grandma. She also shares tips on crafting stunning scarves with Marvelous Designer._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/58c6470b58484b3da8df005678a2765e78edb5aaf247498daf80aa50b10d9147.jpg)

# **We'd like to get to know you better, can you tell us a little about yourself and how you got started in 3D?**

Hello. I'm Geumbi Seo, a junior character modeler from South Korea.

I started studying 3D because I found it fascinating to create things that I love and keep for a long time.

# **Can you tell us more about your latest project, "My Grandma"?**

I became interested in creating realistic characters while taking classes at an academy, and naturally, I thought of my family first, especially my beloved grandma and grandpa. It always broke my heart to see their time go by faster than ours, and as I got older, it always made me sad to imagine a future without them.

So I started a project called “My Grandma” to use the 3D skills I've learned to preserve them in their healthiest and most beautiful state.

As I worked on it, I wanted the others to feel her love through my project. I hope it will inspire each of us to pick up the phone and call or reminisce about our grandmothers.

# **We love the knot on your scarf using Marvelous Designer. Do you have any advice or tips for people who find it difficult to create ribbons or knots in Marvelous Designer?**

I realized while working on this project that it's not easy to make ribbons or knots.

But I didn't want to change the shape of the scarf just because of its difficulty, so I just kept trying multiple times, and eventually, I got the shape I wanted.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/20ceb081d71f4b2f907b907453417298181b037970f34064a3ff68c9ec74b270.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/5cd762fad9f345eda6f71377349885809e1a026934ed47af9ef819b83ac2f9c0.png)

One tip is to use pins and tacks, and I pinned and moved the process slowly, just like tying a scarf, to get the desired shape, if you don't pin or tack it in between, it will unravel, so it's better to pin the finished part until you get the desired shape.

Also, it's good to start with a high particle distance instead of a low particle distance to get the shape, and then lower the particle distance to get the desired crease.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/ff8ea01e2f5e40d2b33c1010982b0006video_240325-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

# **Can you provide a brief overview of the different tools used in the pipeline?**

To work on the face, I used ZBrush and Maya 2022.

I started by creating the basic shape in Zbrush, then converted it to MetaHuman UVs and detailed it in Zbrush again. For the skin detailing, I used a basic standard to lay the groundwork, and from there I created the skin detailing by flowing and shaping the wrinkles to match the reference as closely as possible.

The cardigan and scarf were created using Marvelous Designer, with any additional wrinkles or shaping done in Zbrush. The hair and cardigan fur were done in Maya XGen, and the textures were done using Substance Painter.

The final render was done in Maya Arnold, UE5 in two places.

# **As you worked on the project, I'm sure there were some favorite and some challenging parts. What was the most enjoyable part for you during the process?**

In my case, the facial details were the most fun and enjoyable part.

I studied the references very carefully to make sure that nothing was awkward or too noticeable when considering the overall picture, and it was fun to see how the face gradually became wrinkled and natural.

I also had great mentors who taught me and gave me a lot of feedback on the likenesses, so it was a valuable process to communicate with them.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/33312ebdb0a64d49990456d06adc1cc9c5f90802a9b4432e84192d41fd316b58.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/a847ed3ab0e94f489f1d096b8a1e6b46b0364a01b8964812ae006c73b0ee7d97.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/98c1935f44b34bd6ad77794b29410ab5/images/3d697fa6e063404d8624ce2046a4a5578d7878df478548cdaea7fcf1461e932c.jpg)

It was the first time I'd ever spent so much time studying someone's face, and I remember thinking, 'This is what my grandmother's nose looks like.

It's so similar to my nose," or "You have a dimple here, that's where my dad and sister's dimples come from," and I had a lot of fun making it.

# **If so, what was the biggest challenge you faced when working on the project?**

Working on this project was my first time using Unreal Engine.

There were a lot of things I didn't know, and it took me a little longer to figure out how to work around it, but it was a great way to get me interested in the changes in 3D work, and I feel like I've learned a lot from it.

# **Finally, do you have any advice for people getting started in 3D art? Career advice, mindset when creating artwork, or anything else.**

I studied 3D art late in life while doing other things, and I started studying at an academy. I've come to realize that the key to my progress lies in finding the right school, connecting with inspiring mentors, and surrounding myself with supportive friends.

And I think it's also important to have a study group with friends to share what you know and learn.

It can be tiring because the process is long, but if you don't give up, you will be rewarded with great results. And even if you don't get good results right away, with each subsequent artwork, you will witness noticeable growth, eventually leading to satisfying results. The teachers who taught me always said that, so I was able to achieve satisfying results.

title: The Swat Warrior Project
content:
## _Alsu Rakhimova has walked us through the SWAT Warrior project, discussing the idea behind the model and explaining how the character's tactical outfit was made using Marvelous Designer._

This article was originally published on [80 Level ](https://80.lv/articles/designing-clothes-for-a-3d-character-in-marvelous-designer/)in English under Artist interview by Alsu Rakhimova. Interview conducted by Arti Sergeev.

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/385161d3239949d9bbaf419432ecb621alsu-rakhimova-3%20%281%29.jpg)

# **Interview with****Alsu Rakhimova****| The SWAT Warrior Project﻿ | 3D Character Artist**

# **The SWAT Warrior Project**

Hi everyone! My name is Alsu, and I am a 3D Character Artist based in Vancouver, currently working for PlayStation Visual Arts studio. Since I joined the company last year, I had an opportunity to work on a very exciting upcoming game. Unfortunately, I cannot share more at the moment, but I am looking forward to it

I created the SWAT Warrior project as my final work for my Advanced term at Think Tank Training Centre in early 2022. My supervisor was Nicolas Niño, who is a great Character Artist. The project was based on the concept by Dia Nak. The whole project took just 11 weeks so it was important for me to learn how to efficiently use the software at my disposal, including Unreal Engine 4 and Marvelous Designer. I created the jacket and the pants in Marvelous Designer.

# **Studying Marvelous Designer**

I was introduced to Marvelous Designer at my school. We had an introductory course taught by Kenzo Nishidate. The interface of the software was very intuitive, so it was easy to quickly create simple assets and start garment simulation. I was very excited when I created my very first asset in Marvelous Designer – a pillow! I was so amazed by the garment simulation that I kept dragging the pillow up and down just to see how it was interacting with the environment. Very soon, I was able to create more complicated assets like buttoned shirts and pants. I think that the cloth simulation of MD is a great help for character artists while creating garments or even accessories like shoes or bags.

# **First Steps**

Before starting any project, I always gather reference images of garments in PureRef to make sure I understand the construction of the garment and the cloth texture. You will need this understanding while building the garment in the software and selecting the fabric preset.

For this character, I gathered a lot of images of SWAT uniforms including tactical vests, belts, leg protectors, etc.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/2a35aedd04de44f09226f48f4d8994f5widen_1840x0.jpg)

Once I have a better idea of how my garment is supposed to look, I create a simple blockout of it in ZBrush. This way, I am getting a better understanding of the overall silhouette and construction of the garment. For tight-fitting clothes like pants, I usually just use the Poly Paint brush to schematically outline the seams, pockets, and zippers on the body base mesh.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/20ce30dd23c44da88ed31e6fc5914051widen_1840x0_%281%29.jpg)

# **Setting Up The Outfit**

The next step is to export the body base mesh to Marvelous Designer and start creating the patterns. There are two ways to do that: you can either create a pattern from scratch (with or without the help of existing pattern images that you can find on Google) or you can divide your ZBrush garment into sections and import them as ‘garment’ to Marvelous Designer. The latter method was demonstrated by Arno Schmitz during The Character Art of Horizon Zero Dawn with Guerrilla Games panel: LINK

There are advantages and disadvantages to both options, so go with the option that works for you.

Tips for beginners:

1\. In order to get the proper folds that fit the garment texture, experiment with different fabric presets.

2\. Take advantage of the symmetry and duplicate your patterns to save time.

3\. Learn the Marvelous Designer shortcuts for a smoother switch between instruments.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/55dfeeb8116b40d7ab4702b55df910e6widen_1840x0_%282%29.jpg)

Once you are happy with the fitting, it is time to start adding smaller details like seam piping, padding, and extra folding. It is important to keep this step last since it would be difficult to make big changes afterward. On top of that, garment simulation with smaller details requires a smaller particle distance, making the simulation process slower.

Tips for beginners:

1\. Use shrinkage warp and weft to create nice small wrinkles on the garment piping

2\. Decrease the particle distance to get better garment simulation results

3\. To make the simulation process faster, try freezing/deactivating the garment pieces that you are not working with right now

4\. Obvious but important advice – save often and keep version of your project just in case.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/3b3355067cb74bca833f02df2fdd9e0fwiden_1840x0_%283%29.jpg)

After the garment is complete in Marvelous Designer, I usually export it back to ZBrush using this method by Outgang to refine some folds and to add missing elements like zipper sliders.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/ee8f807769534f0fa651551d645b4f0awiden_1840x0_%284%29.jpg)

# **Approach to Texturing**

I textured the outfit in Substance 3D Painter trying to stick to a procedural method for as long as possible. This allowed me to quickly change the textures to my liking and even use the textures later as a smart material in my later projects. Here are the main principles that I try to stick to while texturing the outfit:

1\. When it comes to color and roughness variation, you want to start with big-scale adjustments and then move to the smaller ones. The key is to zoom out to see the bigger picture from a distance. This way I check if color/roughness/specular variation is good enough.

2\. Use the combination of procedural and hand-painted approaches. The combination of the two approaches will give a unique look to your textures and will save some time. I use a “Dirt” brush for almost all my hand-painted fixes.

3\. While texturing the character, I use a very neutral Environment Map (Display settings > environment settings > Environment Map: “Soft 1LowContrastFront 2Backs”). It helps me to avoid any color reflections on the textured object.

As soon as you have the base color for the character – put the character in the rendering engine right away and confirm that the scale is right.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/c54419aeac48426c8d095edfeac7abf2widen_1840x0_%285%29.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/c0e7c56899ec462daff22477416d562cwiden_1840x0_%287%29.jpg)

# **Rendering & Presentation**

When presenting the game character in the real-time engine, the texture budgets can lead to some small clothing details looking washed out/blurred. In order to preserve the high fidelity of clothes, I add fabric detail normal to all my shaders.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/e2d6b9336feb460c8b1323193aa5787e65573d9276c65.gif)

# **How to Get Started With Marvelous Designer?**

I would advise beginners to start with the basics – try and create a very simple garment and export it to a different software (Maya, ZBrush, Blender, etc.). It will help you to understand both how the Marvelous Designer UI works and how to integrate it into your workflow. There are a lot of free step-by-step video tutorials that could help you to learn. Personally, I highly recommend such YouTube channels as [Outgang ](https://www.youtube.com/@Outgang/playlists)and [Evgeniia Petrova](https://www.youtube.com/@EvgeniiaPetrova).

# Alsu Rakhimova, 3D Character Artist

# [ _Artist Artstation_](https://www.artstation.com/artdungeon)

Interview conducted by Arti Burton

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/598e4b9d88fb4704b89371d083b9caa2alsu-rakhimova-3%20%281%29.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5441f9b4e35e464d84f8e6307744762b/images/6368571efab742fe9907edc940df55a5alsu-rakhimova-3%20%281%29.jpg)

## _Discover a wealth of insights with Sana, from intricate details to unique workflows for character design._

* * *

# Interview with Sana Almusalli | Drift﻿ | 3D Character Artist

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/7e6b41b2bb3240c98f1026bdc35e957101%20%281%29.jpg)

# **We'd like to learn more about you. Can you introduce yourself and how did you first get started in 3D?**

Hi everyone! My name is Sana Almusalli Alawadhi and I am an Emirati 3D Character Artist. I have always been into art but never knew which direction to go. I used to think 2D art was what I wanted to do in the future but once I started experimenting with 3D art, I absolutely fell in love and have been creating 3D art since.

To further learn and enhance my skills, I enrolled in DAE to study Game Graphic Production. Once I graduated, I enrolled with Think Tank Training Centre to study at their online Character Art Program to advance in character creation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/2222b250170a48a9907bdd72ab4c751702.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/4d8536fc37d449729922b4cd670cc5f8ezgif-1-c2bcc4850f.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/7accd553d9064afdb641cc5e80c6fad1ezgif-1-9bd337f4ca.webp)

# **Can you provide details on your project: Drift?**

Drift was my mentorship project that I created from a concept art by CABORO. I had fallen in love with the concept and had saved the image for a while before I ended up re-creating it for my mentorship program with the help of my mentor Denis Melenets.

During the mentorship, I got the chance to experiment with a number of different aspects related to character creation. For example, I experimented with hair creation, body and clothes animation, and head blend shape animation with Unreal Engine, which I had been eager to do for a while.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/56241dc33c1043779c0b61102091082bezgif-1-ce00e8f2c1.webp)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

I used various programs to create the project. I used Zbrush and Marvelous Designer for the creation of the initial block out and for the final high poly. I also used Blender for Subdivision and Boolean modeling. I then used Rizom UV for the UV and Marmoset Toolbag and Substance painter for the bake and texture. I also used Maya to create the Xgen hair and finally used Unreal Engine to render.

In addition to those programs, I also used a base mesh from 3D Scan Store to help me quicken the process of creating the character sculpt and Quixel Bridge to help me create the environment for the final presentation

# **What are the biggest challenges that you face during projects?**

As I like to experiment a lot, I usually end up facing different challenges with every character. For the project Drift, one of my biggest challenges was creating the twists of the hair and working on an already posed character. Since I was trying to do a posed character, I decided to create the outfit on a non-posed character at first and once I was happy with the design and how it looked, I was ready to move on to simulating a posed character.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/3b6458f81b2b4430be3646e3bf01880106_beforeAnim.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/8c3b153aef3b44cd8b47d73b3bb53c4707_afterAnim.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/b0e39d0dbcb546a9ba0f1604934ed4f1ezgif-1-c1ba8b05df.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/188bdb436de04d5b8e41ff45ab743dbd/images/343ac3069555454f89b78fa3042522d309.webp)

Another big challenge I faced was how I could create the blend shape for the head so that I could create various expressions while making sure the XGen hair follows the head and eyes of the character.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

I love using Marvelous Designer since it helps me create realistic looking outfits and experiment with different materials and designs with ease and with little time. I love learning about the technical part of Marvelous Designer as there are a lot of useful elements that I use to either fasten my workflow or make the outfit look even better.

As I was also able to join a class by Jayson Fitch at CGMA, I learnt most of the techniques about Marvelous Designer from that class. A few things that I always love to use are the pinning and freezing features for when I am happy with a certain area of the fabric while I work on the rest. The GPU Simulation feature is another feature that I love to use, as well as the Fabric Physical Properties that I can use to adjust the outfits to further match the concept art.

One thing I am really intrigued by is to experiment with rigging and animating clothes. I would love to learn how to rig more complex outfits for game characters. I am also looking into more realistic moveable outfits along with possibly using blend shapes.

# **Lastly, what advice do you have for someone looking to get started in the industry?**

I started to improve the more I researched and experimented with new workflows and techniques. That's why I would suggest that others use as many resources as possible. I love using Youtube, Gumroad, Flipped Normals to find tutorials that are helpful for each project. Another thing that helps me is keeping notes of any issues or problems that I come across and the solution for the problem as well. This has been especially helpful since I can come back to the notes if I ever come across the same or a similar issue again, and since I use PureRef for this, I find it even more helpful as I can add lots of pictures to come back to it again and easily find the notes in the future.

## _Discover the exclusive behind-the-scenes journey of Marvelous Designer's contribution to Half M.T studio's award-winning project, 'The Voice in the Hollow,' which proudly received the Jury Award at the 2023 Siggraph._

* * *

# **Interview with Half M.T Studios | The Voice in the Hollow﻿**

# **Introduction: Interviewee Artist & Half M.T Studios**

I'm Miguel Ortega, a director and VFX supervisor at Half M.T Studios in Los Angeles, California. The studio, co-founded by Tran Ma and myself, gets its name from us - Half Miguel, Half Tran. Recently, we completed "The Voice in the Hollow," an African Animated Horror film rendered in Unreal Engine 5. We made this film with a small team, backed by the support of Gnomon.

# **Congratulations on the winning of the Jury Award at SIGGRAPH 2023! Can you tell us more about the project: 'VOICE IN THE HOLLOW'?**

We're really honored to have won that award. I've been attending Siggraph ever since I was a student at Gnomon, which is over 18 years now. Getting an award from them means a lot to us. "The Voice in the Hollow" is a horror film we made completely in Swahili. It centers on two sisters and their jealousy. We managed to wrap it up in just 10 months, during the last part of the COVID pandemic.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in our film. We mainly used Megascans assets, tweaking them into something entirely new. But with Marvelous Designer, we found we could add a lot of complexity to our sets without much effort. Fabric created in Marvelous Designer looks real, intricate, and beautiful, and it's surprisingly easy to work with. This was a game-changer for Tran, our lead Marvelous Designer artist. She was able to quickly bring a wide range of fabric details into our scenes, adding depth and realism in a short amount of time.

On top of enhancing our sets, we also used Marvelous Designer for all our characters' clothing. It was a straightforward process to design and simulate the cloth entirely within Marvelous Designer. This tool really streamlined the way we brought our characters to life, giving them a more authentic and dynamic look with minimal hassle.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/279708ec76a24b89b28ef347ca97a240wip_03%20%281%29.jpg)

# **Could you give us examples of some iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for?**

My favorite scenes where we used Marvelous Designer are definitely the ceremony sequence and the final fight. In the ceremony scene, I got the set to a point where it looked pretty good, but then Tran came in and just elevated it. She added fabric everywhere - hanging from the ceiling, wrapped around bones, laid out as rugs - and it looked incredible.

For the final fight, using Marvelous Designer really added to the drama. We turned up the wind effects, so the characters' clothes were dramatically flapping in the wind, which I loved. It brought so much intensity to the scene. And all of this was designed and simulated in Marvelous Designer, which shows how powerful the tool can be.

# **We know that VOICE IN THE HOLLOW is successfully made with Unreal Engine 5. Can you give us a quick overview of your pipeline involving Marvelous Designer, Unreal Engine 5, and other tools?**

Since we're a small team, finding the easiest and fastest methods is crucial for us. We discovered that using Alembic caches worked best for our workflow. Our process started with animating the characters in Maya. Then, we did shot modeling to address any deformation issues. After that, these models were brought into Marvelous Designer.

In Marvelous Designer, we'd create the cloth simulations, and then export them as Alembic (.ABC) files back to Maya. There, we reassigned the material properties before finally moving everything into Unreal Engine.

I'm sure there might be simpler ways to do this, but with our approach, we were able to turn around a shot in just minutes. This speed and efficiency were vital for our project's success, given our team's size.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/969f36367f0b41d0b48939f57cf3e080ezgif-2-1aa218adc7.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/9ef6355a6fab43baae37cc508b4f37b7ezgif-2-4dda8b3277.webp)

# **We saw that the characters' clothes are animated in Marvelous Designer. Were there any challenges when you animated characters' clothes in Marvelous Designer? How did you overcome the challenges?**

After we had a basic concept for the clothing in Marvelous Designer but before fully rigging the characters, we would first import the naked model into Mixamo, the free online rigging application. There, we applied basic running or jumping motion capture animations. This step allowed us to then bring these animated models back into Marvelous Designer, now with the clothing applied.

At this stage, while the character deformations weren't perfect, it was a critical point for us to identify any potential issues in the clothing simulations. We were constantly balancing between what looked visually appealing and what performed well in the simulation. If the clothing simulation didn't act as we anticipated, we'd adjust the costume design until it matched our expectations. This method was a practical way to ensure that the clothing would look good and behave realistically in the final animation, without having to wait for the characters to be fully rigged.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/6e91fe93e0984a6ca321e7135b43972cVITH_presentation.033%20%281%29.jpg)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community for animators?**

​​A lot of what we've learned comes from Megan's (from the marvelous designer channel) incredible tutorials on YouTube. She's a fantastic resource, and I definitely recommend checking her out if you want to learn from the best. Also, every Friday at 1 PM PST, we do a live stream on the Gnomon YouTube channel. In these sessions, we dive into the process behind our current film. We're experimenting with Marvelous Designer in some pretty unconventional ways, especially using it for architectural details, which is turning out to be quite extraordinary.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

We absolutely love Marvelous Designer; it's been a game-changer for our work. Our passion for it has inspired our latest project, where we've created an entire world made of fabric. Every detail, from the spoons and forks to the intricate Art Nouveau architecture, is crafted in Marvelous Designer. This project, a testament to the versatility and power of Marvelous Designer, wouldn't have been possible without our deep commitment to exploring the full potential of this tool. So thank you guys!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/753b9aa085e24c279ab4e01b8837d962the_threadings%20%281%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/e97a0f2d6a19439cba6cbdc5d1ec0292/images/1b81b585bee04bf4ad941ff388177f6cmaxresdefault%20%2833%29.jpg)
content_description: Explore how Marvelous Designer empowered Half M.T Studios to create award-winning fabric simulations and dynamic character clothing in their Siggraph 2023 Jury Award-winning film, *The Voice in the Hollow*.

## _Eugene shares the behind-the-scenes story of Marvelous Designer's involvement in her short animation, "The Antique"_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/950ac101ff9c40a9a235593b0103b866/images/2ee5f69a338c4c14ad4a991e587fc203%ED%99%94%EB%A9%B4%20%EC%BA%A1%EC%B2%98%202024-12-10%20180831.png)

<https://vimeo.com/823293011>

# **Artist Introduction**

Hi, my name is Eugene Jung - working as a 3D motion graphics designer. I have a desire to create character animations myself, so I'm consistently studying and working on character-related projects personally.

# **Tell us about the animation project: The Antique.**

"The Antique" is a short animation depicting 'Yeon,' who operates a vintage goods store, preparing for the store's opening. I started the production with the idea of creating a video filled with things I like. The work aims to portray vintage items, a warm sunny atmosphere, and relaxing morning hours.

# **We'd like to hear more about the art direction in the costume of Yeon. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

I envisioned the season within "The Antique" transitioning from winter to spring. Throughout the video, I aimed for a casual yet warm feeling in the chosen clothing that complements the sunlight coming through the windows. I wanted the attire to be comfortable yet convey a sense of intimacy. Therefore, I ultimately opted for a cardigan and jeans in the video, incorporating bright spring colors to create a fresh and lively atmosphere.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve in your animation project?**

I believe that expressing the natural movement of hair and clothing plays a key in conveying the vitality of a character, so I pay close attention to this aspect when working. In the case of "The Antique," where the character takes center stage, achieving a natural flow in the clothing movement was important. Utilizing Marvelous Designer allowed me to depict the natural movement of the clothing, enabling me to effectively capture the vitality of the character as I envisioned throughout the entire video.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline including Marvelous Designer?**

# [Planning]

I collect references for tone, mood, the protagonist's appearance, and clothing. I then organize the storyline in written form. Based on the script, I create storyboards and produce style frames for essential scenes in the video. During this process, I use Marvelous Designer to test the feel of the clothing.

# [Video Editing]

After roughing out the major movements of the camera and characters in 3D, I proceed to overall video editing. Once I confirm that the video length and composition are seamless, I delve into detailed animation.

# [Cloth Simulation]

Upon completion of the animation, I import the character into Marvelous Designer to simulate the clothing. The costumes created in Marvelous Designer are further refined in Substance Painter to craft intricate clothing textures.

# [Finalizing]

After final adjustments to the look, I proceed to render, composite, and edit the background music, concluding the video production process.

# **Could you give examples of some of the iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for in “The Antique”?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/950ac101ff9c40a9a235593b0103b866/images/04c97dee5ad04aaa9cce20c436a6c616a005090f2f31422fa2fbf5ede4e1fd0b%20%281%29.png)

Here are the initial scenes featuring Yeon, the first being the panoramic shot and the subsequent mirror scene. The panoramic scene reveals Yeon's full body, and it was crucial to simulate the clothing's natural movement as she walks. In the mirror scene, Marvelous Designer was used for the floral-patterned curtains, lace on the shelf, and the moving curtains reflected in the mirror, as well as the tablecloth.

With Marvelous Designer, I could achieve a natural movement for the curtains swaying in the wind and the tablecloth, enhancing the overall realism of these scenes.

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

I tend to purchase project files from the Marvelous Designer Asset Store (CONNECT) and external markets (such as ArtStation) when needed, and I use them after making adjustments to fit the characters.

In this project as well, I bought a project file, modified it to suit the character, and incorporated it into the workflow.

By taking a reference to how other designers create patterns and sew using Marvelous Designer, I've been able to enhance my understanding of the software. It provides valuable insights into different approaches and techniques employed by fellow designers, contributing to an overall improvement in my proficiency with Marvelous Designer.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer allows for the quick production of high-quality garments within a short period. Not only that, but it also makes it very easy to achieve a realistic feel of fabric. Additionally, there is a wealth of tutorials and both free and paid items available for users, making it quite accessible even for those unfamiliar with Marvelous Designer. This enables users to easily utilize only the necessary features, even without extensive knowledge of the software.

[Link to Behance](https://www.behance.net/withorwithout)

[Link to Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/withorwithoutx/)

title: Making An Armor In Marvelous Designer: Breaking Boundaries
content:
## _Meet Sarah, a skilled 3D designer, as she unveils her process for crafting hard-surface armor using Marvelous Designer. The hard surface look is seamlessly achieved within the creative realm of Marvelous Designer._

* * *

# **Interview with Sarah Prado | Armor Creation in MD | 3D artist**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/30efa36ca78444c980c8506dcd6a44dd2733c7e3de954fbcb3d558d99ff94578.png)

# **Artist Introduction.**

My name is Sarah, I am a Brazilian 3D Artist, Fashion Designer, gamer, and mother of cats. I have a university degree in Fashion and for more than 10 years I worked as a designer, patternmaker, and seamstress in local industries, mainly with bridal gowns and formal wear for women.

I had my first experience with Marvelous in 2020 during the Covid lockdown, which has blown my mind. Since then I have fully migrated to 3D, where I can work with more fantastic designs and test patterns for much less expense and much less waste.

Nowadays I use mainly Marvelous, Substance Painter, and Blender.

Although one can apply Marvelous into to a range of areas such as home decor and stylized characters, I really enjoy working with realistic but fantastic designs.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/47381740a2d046839a26fbfdfbe2add5sorceress%20isometric.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/76f1edc7c11b4a318b0bb57004547425cathedral%20render3-front2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/3200103c62c24e228272db1d2e6a67ddcathedral%20render3-back2.png)

# **You've recently released impressive armor creations that have received a tremendous response from the user community. We are extremely curious to know what inspired you to implement armor creation that can be created on hard surfaces in other software. Can you tell us more?﻿**

﻿This artwork in particular came from this annoying situation that older gamer girls would face when playing RPG and fantasy genre when the armor supposed to protect the character's body is actually more like a bikini made of steel and sheer fabric. So I made a meme-like expectation vs reality artwork. It was fun and I enjoyed how both versions ended up, but I put much more time and research into the realistic one.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/1fdd42fb51714dae9d01020023fa6842expectation%20x%20reality2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/9b3ec971b5014c318e0dd64919e59938armor%20ref.png)

# **What was your primary focus in your artwork? What are the powerful benefits of making armor using Marvelous Designer?**

It is kind of a personal challenge since I was told I could nor should do any of the sort in clothing simulation software. So I've been playing with adding hard-surface elements totally made into Marvelous in previous artworks before the armor with great results even when simulating animation and the main reason for that is: I'm a total noob in other programs.

As a fashion designer, I guess I'm more functional thinking in clothing patterns than as a sculptor. I have no idea if a blacksmith would use cut pieces of flat metal to bend and weld into armor, but that's definitely what I would do. I think that's what cosplay makers do, anyway.

So, why not? People come from different backgrounds and I think we all should be allowed to go after the results we want no matter the tool we are more comfortable with!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f02d686156544563a2db50a39230c4faarmor%20marvelous.png)

# **Would you be able to provide us with an overview of your pipeline, focusing on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

Of course! It's basically a fabric with stiffer but smooth aspect presets (high shear, high bending, medium stretch, etc) and fold angles.

I like starting with an avatar in A-pose, where I make a doublet: a regular fabric garment usually worn under the armor. I keep it single-layered since most of the reverse won't be shown, the sewn lines are actually internal lines with fold angles over 180.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/7715e9b907d244d5a7da85066f035733step1.png)

Then I add the patterns to be the armor itself, I like to start with a Trim Full Grain Leather fabric and then tweak its properties until it reaches the desired hardness.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/8c308fd6f361446aad510aa61916fefastep2.png)

To keep the armor pieces attached one to another I use internal lines to emulate rivets or links. I may model some leather stripes to attach the metal pieces too. It will serve as a guide later when texturing to make it look like a rivet.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f06bc6ff50fd437ebfb81e5387a193e7step3.png)

  
That done, I go to designing the surface angles using internal lines and changing the fold angles too, <180 for the pinch effect and >180 for creases. Some designs will need several internal lines and different fold angles. It may be needed to apply fold angles on the sewing lines too. That's what will make the sculpted appearance of the metal plates. Fold angles only show in 3D when simulating in "normal" or "fitting" modes, "fast" mode does not deliver a good result.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/424f8901080b49eab71c0421e1342b2fstep4.png)

Depending on the piece, it also should be necessary to apply bond or seam tapings ("under the collar" preset is great for this) and, after reaching the desired shape, solidify so it stays in place.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/769a5db341de4247b5134d5a12bf02a0step5.png)

Last but not least, I like to play with the thickness too. Usually, I lower the curved side geometry or even remove it to keep it more angular.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/ac61a436bc224a6cb8df73e186c81f44step6.png)

  
That's the essence of how I make armor and hard-surface elements using Marvelous!

The only challenge I faced was that I had to adapt the patterns to visually fit what I wanted.

For example, the cords that fasten the vambraces were not really long cords but little pieces sewn in the right places; the buckles were not really buckles but hard fabric cut in the right shapes. It doesn't need to be, just needs to look like it is. Anything else just required patience and creativity to shape the design.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/f468b275282443648dc65289f82ee263step7.png)

  


# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

There's one I like: for some pieces when you need to have a gap, for example, a corset backside or a deep neckline you want to keep in place, just make a piece of pattern fitting the gap and sew to the piece borders, then when simulating it will not show any pressure points or deformations. Deactivate (pattern only) and hide the 3D view of this pattern. You'll then have a gap with straight borders and the hidden piece will not be exported with your object!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d4b3d81d36b4b1f976cbfb3db7a3342/images/82ef2d9ff83f4a2a953e3dbb5a7a499dtip%20final.png)

If you need to simulate an animation then you'll have to activate it, but it may face some instabilities then. Testing is the key.

## UPP reveals the spacecraft production techniques   
from the movie "Voyagers". Marvelous Designer played a crucial role in crafting realistic spaceships.

* * *

# **Interview with UPP | Voyager | VFX Studio**

# **Could you introduce your studio?**

UPP is an international VFX and Post Production Studio. Since its establishment in 1994, UPP has become one of the largest and most versatile Visual Effects and Post Production Houses in Mainland Europe. With teams in Prague and Budapest, we work with filmmakers and clients from all over the world.

# **Could you briefly introduce the project: Voyagers?**

The Voyagers Project is about a crew of astronauts on a multi-generational mission descending into paranoia and madness, unable to determine what is real and what isn't.

Directed by: Neil Burger

Produced by: Basil Iwanyk, Neil Burger, Brendon Boyea

Stars: Colin Farrell, Tye Sheridan, Fionn Whitehead and Lily-Rose Depp

# **Can you explain how Marvelous Designer was used for the spacesuit and its impact on this project?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/8847c06992974840a2af9e4ec7339e3eezgif-1-9b2343fb57.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/351a094442c4488f97362fe39aed2691ezgif-1-5e02c636c0.webp)

When we created the spacesuit in a bag for the Voyager project, we based it on a photogrammetric scan.We created the spacesuit in a bag in individual layers.

Our goal was to approach the production as efficiently as possible, therefore we produced the entire asset, except for small details, in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/cfe5933821034cda8b9e41ea4a44a4c5UPP_2.webp)

# **Apart from the spacesuit, which other objects were created using Marvelous Designer?**

We also used Marvelous Designer to easily create the fabric covering the spaceship's hull.

Below we will present a series of images that present step-by-step how the cloth pieces were created for a specific piece that is part of the spaceship.

  * **Collision model of the structure under the cloth - Creation of basic parts of the cloth - UV layout of the basic cloth parts**


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/44a60eead4c746ad91f2dd7246724b48ssClothA_md_01_objectForDynamics.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/5dd8c92a97fd4c09b85687bb99007e75ssClothA_md_02_partsCreated.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/04e1971e47a142ff95e6555ca4edeafessClothA_md_03_partsUVs.webp)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/dd81684c70794478881b27a5d635caf9ssClothA_md_07_pressureAdded.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f67f96b7bed944fa970b32945e988e69ssClothA_md_09_pinResult.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/f464f33ca44d4205a745fa6c50b3b125ssClothA_md_10_tubesAdded.webp)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/cc2a0a70172e44ef944cf6c48f40ad16ssClothC_render_04_shade.webp)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/1654abab8e824b3baa80aa6fb676500dssClothC_render_05_final.webp)

# **Do you recommend using Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer is an incredibly user-friendly software thanks to its many features. One of the most important is the ability to freeze and deactivate patterns, which allows you to speed up simulations and create more complex patterns. It is also possible to create patterns directly on an avatar or import OBJ as a garment.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b665ad057db742da859c503f444622aa/images/3feb4edbcf9941c6b0f0c1b923407012spaceship_3.webp)
